text.p: These are the highlights in the Bosnian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- U.S. Assistant Secretary of State John Shattuck warned Mostar officials during his visit to Bosnia that the international community will not support authorities which systematically obstruct the return of refugees. Shattuck met Moslem officials but Croat representatives failed to turn up for the meeting.

- The Moslem chairman of the Bosnian presidency and Croatian President Franjo Tudjman will discuss two agreements signed last year in Zagreb at their meeting scheduled for August 6 in Split. The agreements govern the use of the port of Ploce for the Moslem-Croat federation side and travel through the coastal town of Neum, says federation foreign trade minister Hasan Muratovic.

- A pulmonary care clinic with angiography equipment opened in Tuzla and will be the only such centre for cardio-vascular treatment in Bosnia. Financial assistance was provided by the U.S. University of Buffalo.

- A Turkish ship transporting 659 tons of weapons, ammunition and military equipment -- including Leopard tanks -- for the Moslem-Croat federation army arrived Saturday at the port of Ploce as part of U.S.-sponsored "equip and train" programme.

- Bosnia will need $400 million for 1997 and 1998 to cover balance of payments and servicing of external debt, the International Monetary Fund said in a statement presented at last week's donors' conference.
- Everything that falls outside the Dayton peace agreement means another war in Bosnia, prime minister of Bosnia's Serb republic, Gojko Klickovic, says in an interview.
- The constutional court of the Serb republic will decide on August 10 about the legality of President Biljana Plavsic's decision to disband the Serb assembly.

- There have been violent incidents in the southern town of Mostar since the establishment of the nationally-balanced Moslem-Croat joint police force last week, Mostar police report said. --Sarajevo newsroom +387 71 663 384
